cards.title: Should You Try the '18 Summers' Parenting Trend?
cards.body: Long days with nothing to do is the whole point of summer, not a 'making memories' exercise. Turning school holidays into controlled activities can feel creepy and controlling to children.

cards.title: Orangutans Arrange Playdates—What Parents Can Learn
cards.body: Scientists say messing about and playdates have real health benefits for humans of all ages. Parents facing six weeks of summer childcare can take inspiration from how orangutans engage their offspring.

cards.title: Is Your Son Defiant or Missing a Skill?
cards.body: What looks like defiance is usually a boy lacking the executive functioning skills the moment demands. This is how to help sons build those essential skills.

cards.title: When Your Child's Meltdown Means You're Winning
cards.body: If your child's tantrums got worse right after you started doing everything right, you haven't failed. You've almost won—this is often a sign of progress in behavior change.

cards.title: What to Do When Your Child's Teacher Is Unfair
cards.body: When adults are unfair to your child, it might be a great learning opportunity instead of a disaster you need to correct. Let your child navigate some unfairness to build resilience.

cards.title: Managing Advocacy Burnout for Neurodivergent Children
cards.body: As back-to-school approaches, parents of neurodivergent children should be mindful about advocacy burnout. Learn tips to care for yourself while supporting your child's needs.
